evidence: Cic. Off. 1.13: vērī inquīsītiō atque investīgātiō

terms.comment: Properly to follow a track, as a hound does (ad investīgandum sagācitās nārium, Cic. ND 2.158, Lewis & Short).

evidence: Cic. Off. 1.15: indāgātiō atque inventiō vērī (Lewis & Short)

phrases.latin: in prīmīsque hominis est propria vērī inquīsītiō atque investīgātiō
phrases.english: above all, it is proper to man to search for the truth and to research it

phrases.latin: Nihil tam difficile est quīn quaerendō investīgārī possiet.
phrases.english: Nothing is so hard that it can’t be found out by looking.

sources: Lewis & Short: investigatio · Lewis & Short: investigo · Lewis & Short: indagatio
Morgan–Owens, Adumbratio: s.v. research (scientific).
John C. Traupman, Conversational Latin for Oral Proficiency, pp. 31, 370.
Quotations from the Latinitas loci collections (loci-cicero-philosophica, loci-terentius), checked against the editions named there.
